# Volume 2 — XI Facts and Fancies

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Educating pupils is actually quite an engaging job,” Nell penned in a letter to a friend from Regent’s Academy. “Odette mentions that she considers it tedious, yet my experience differs. Nearly every day, some humorous event is likely to occur, and the statements from the boys and girls are so entertaining. Odette states that her students receive punishment whenever they utter humorous remarks, a practice that likely explains why she perceives instruction as dull. Earlier today, young Jimmy Pullen attempted to spell ‘speckled’ without success. ‘Well,’ he uttered at last, ‘I can’t spell it but I know what it means.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0000 }

“‘Say again?’ I inquired.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0001 }

“‘The face of St. Clair Trask, miss.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0002 }

“St. Clair does have a great deal of freckles, even though I endeavor to stop the rest from making remarks about them . . . because I had freckles at one time and my memory of it is vivid. However, I believe St. Clair is unbothered. The reason St. Clair thrashed Jimmy while returning from school was that Jimmy addressed him as ‘St. Clair’. Word of the thrashing reached me, though not through official channels, which leads me to believe I should ignore the matter.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0003 }

“I was attempting to instruct Lottie Duckett in adding numbers yesterday. I inquired, ‘If you had three candies in one hand and two in the other, how many would you have altogether?’ Lottie responded, ‘A mouthful.’ Furthermore, during nature study, upon my requesting a valid justification for not destroying toads, Benjie Mott solemnly replied, ‘Because it would rain the next day.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0004 }

“Mabel, refraining from laughter is extremely difficult. All my amusement must be kept inside until I return home, and Thirza claims that hearing unprovoked, wild shrieks of mirth coming from the east gable makes her uneasy. According to her, a man in Welby lost his mind once, and those very sounds marked the start of it.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0005 }

“Were you aware of the fact that Thomas a Becket was made a saint as a snake? According to Rose Bell, he was . . . and she also claims William Tyndale authored the New Testament. Claude White asserts that a ‘glacier’ means a person who installs window frames!
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0006 }

“I believe that drawing out the children’s genuine ideas on various subjects is both the hardest and the most fascinating part of instruction. During a tempestuous day this past week, I brought them together around myself at lunchtime and attempted to have them speak with me precisely as though I were their peer. I requested that they share the items they desired above all else. A few of the responses were rather ordinary . . . skates, ponies, and dolls. Other requests were quite unique. Dinah Gammon wished ‘to wear her Sunday dress every day and eat in the sitting room.’ Hannah Bell desired ‘to be good without having to take any trouble about it.’ Marjory White, who is ten years old, wished to be a widow. When I asked her reason, she solemnly remarked that people named you an old maid if you lacked a husband, whereas your husband commanded you if you had one; however, neither hazard existed for a widow. Sally Bell possessed the most extraordinary desire. She desired a ‘honeymoon.’ I inquired whether she understood what that meant, and she replied that she assumed it was a particularly fine sort of bicycle, since her Montreal cousin embarked on a honeymoon upon getting married, and he had invariably owned the newest style of bicycles!
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0007 }

“On a different day, I requested that everyone inform me of the most wicked action they had ever committed. Although I was unable to persuade the older children to comply, the third class responded with complete openness. Eliza Bell had ‘set fire to her aunt’s carded rolls.’ When I questioned whether she intended to accomplish this, she replied, ‘not altogether.’ She merely tested a tiny tip to observe its burning, and the entire package caught fire instantly. Emerson Pettigrew had expended a dime on sweets when he ought to have placed it inside his missionary box. The most severe offense of Annetta Bell was ‘eating some blueberries that grew in the graveyard.’ Willie White had ‘slid down the sheephouse roof a lot of times with his Sunday trousers on.’ ‘But I was punished for it ’cause I had to wear patched pants to Sunday School all summer, and when you’re punished for a thing you don’t have to repent of it,’ Willie asserted.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0008 }

“How I desire that you might view a few of their writings . . . my longing is such that I intend to forward duplicates of several produced not long ago. The previous week, I instructed the fourth class to compose epistles to me regarding whatever topic they chose, proposing as an idea that they could describe a location they had journeyed to or a fascinating object or individual they had encountered. These communications were to be penned on actual stationery, enclosed within an envelope, and directed to my name, entirely unassisted by anyone else. This past Friday forenoon, a collection of missives awaited me upon my desk, and later that night, I was reminded anew that instruction yields delight alongside its hardships. Those pieces of writing could compensate for a great deal. Below is the one by Ned Clay, with the location, orthography, and syntax preserved precisely as first written.”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0009 }

“‘Miss schoolmistress ShiRley Green gabels. p.e. Island are birds capable
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0010 }

“‘Dear teacher I believe I shall compose a essay for you regarding birds. birds are extremely helpful creatures. my cat captures birds. He is named William although pa names him tom. he is entirely striped and last winter he had one of his ears froz off. if not for that he would be a handsome cat. My unkle has taken in a cat. it arrived at his house one day and would not leave and unkle states it has forgotten more than the majority of people ever knowed. he allows it to sleep in his rocking chare and my aunt remarks he cares more for it than he does for his children. that is incorrect. we should treat cats kindly and offer them new milk but we should not treat them better than our children. this is oll I am able to think of so nothing further at present from
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0011 }

edward blake ClaY.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0012 }

“St. Clair Trask’s, as per usual, is brief and direct. Words are never wasted by St. Clair. I don't believe that malice aforethought drove his choice of subject or the addition of the postscript. Rather, he simply lacks much tact or imagination.”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0013 }

“‘Dear Miss Harcourt
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0014 }

“‘We were instructed by you to detail a peculiar thing that we have observed. My description will be of the Brierley Hall. Its doors number two, comprising an inner one alongside an outer one. Six windows are present on it, as well as a chimney. A pair of ends and a pair of sides belong to it. Blue is the color it is painted. That circumstance renders it strange. The lower Delford road is where it is constructed. Among the structures in Brierley, its importance ranks third. The church together with the blacksmith shop constitute the others. Debating clubs, in addition to lectures and concerts, are conducted within it.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0015 }

“‘Truly yours, “‘Jacob Trask.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0016 }

“‘P.S. The color of the hall is a most vivid blue.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0017 }

“The length of Annetta Bell’s missive astonished me, because composing compositions is hardly Annetta’s strong suit, and her usual attempts are just as short as St. Clair’s. Although Annetta is a reserved small creature and an exemplar of fine deportment, she possesses not a trace of inventiveness. This is what she wrote.—
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0018 }

“‘Most beloved educator,
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0019 }

“‘I believe I shall compose a missive to you describing the depth of my affection. My love for you encompasses my entire heart, soul, and mind . . . every part of me that is capable of loving . . . and my desire is to be of service to you eternally. To do so would be my greatest honor. This explains my intense effort to behave properly at school and master my lessuns.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0020 }

“‘You possess such beauty, my teacher. The sound of your voice resembles music, and your eyes look like dew-covered pansies. You bring to mind a tall, majestic queen. Rippling gold is what your hair looks like. Anthony Tulk claims that it is red, but Anthony does not deserve any of your attention.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0021 }

“‘Although we met merely a handful of months ago, I am unable to conceive that a period existed wherein you were unknown to me . . . before you entered my existence to bestow upon it blessing and sanctity. This year will forever remain in my memory as the most marvelous of my existence, for it delivered you to my side. Furthermore, it marks the time of our relocation to Brierley from Stonebridge. The affection I hold for you has rendered my existence profoundly abundant, shielding me from a great deal of injury and wickedness. Every bit of this is owed to you, my most beloved instructor.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0022 }

“‘I will always remember how lovely you appeared when I last beheld you wearing that dark gown adorned with blossoms in your hair. That is how I will picture you eternally, even once we have both grown elderly and hoary. To me, my most beloved instructor, you shall perpetually remain youthful and beautiful. My thoughts are constantly filled with you. . . as day breaks, at midday, and during the evening light. My affection for you remains whether you are smiling or lamenting . . . even if your expression appears contemptuous. I have never observed a vexed look on your face, although Anthony Tulk claims that is your perpetual expression, yet I am not surprised you appear vexed toward him because he merits it. My love for you persists in all attire . . . with every additional gown, you appear even more delightful than before.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0023 }

“‘My most beloved instructor, I wish you a good night. Nightfall has arrived and the stars have begun to gleam . . . stars possessing a brilliance and beauty matching your own eyes. I press my lips to your hands and your face, my darling. May the Almighty guard you and shield you against every danger.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0024 }

“‘Your afecksionate pupil, “‘Annetta Bell.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0025 }

“I was quite perplexed by this remarkable letter. That Annetta was no more capable of writing it than she was of flying was something I knew. The following day at school, I escorted her to the brook during recess and requested that she share the truth concerning the letter with me. Crying, Annetta readily confessed. She stated that she had not written a letter before, possessed no knowledge of how to do so or what to express, but her mother’s top bureau drawer contained a package of love letters that an old ‘beau’ had sent to her mother.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0026 }

“‘Father wasn’t the one,’ wept Annetta, ‘a person studying to be a minister was, which meant his letters were written beautifully, yet ma ended up not marrying him. Half the time, she said she had no idea what he meant. However, I found those letters sweet, so I decided to merely transcribe parts of them now and then for my letters to you. Where he had written “lady,” I inserted “teacher,” and whenever an idea came to me, I added my own thoughts, along with changing a few words. Instead of “mood,” I wrote “dress.” What a “mood” actually was eluded me, though I assumed it was an article of clothing. It never occurred to me that you would spot the difference. How you discovered it was not entirely my own work baffles me. Teacher, you have to be extremely clever.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0027 }

“I expressed to Annetta that copying someone else’s letter to pretend it was hers was extremely improper. However, I fear that the only thing Annetta regretted was getting caught.”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0028 }

“‘And I really love you, teacher,’ she cried. ‘Even though the minister wrote it beforehand, it was all true. I love you with my entire heart.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0029 }

“Chastising someone effectively becomes extremely hard when you are in a situation like this.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0030 }

“Barbara Shaw’s letter is right here. The original’s inkblots cannot be reproduced by me.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0031 }

”‘Beloved instructor,
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0032 }

“‘You mentioned that we could write concerning a visit. I have only ever visited one time. It occurred at my Aunt Mary’s during the previous winter. My Aunt Mary is an extremely particular woman as well as a great housekeeper. On the initial night of my stay, we were having tea. I tipped over a jug and it broke. Aunt Mary stated that she had possessed that jug continuously since her marriage and no one had ever broken it previously. Upon getting up, I trod on her dress and every gather tore away from the skirt. On the following morning, as I rose from bed, I struck the pitcher against the basin, cracking the pair of them, and I spilled a cup of tea onto the tablecloth during breakfast. While I was assisting Aunt Mary with the dishes from dinner, I dropped a china plate and it shattered. That same evening, I tumbled down the stairs and sprained my ankle, forcing me to remain in bed for a week. I overheard Aunt Mary telling Uncle Joseph that it was a blessing, otherwise I would have destroyed every single thing inside the house. By the time I recovered, it was time for me to return home. I do not enjoy visiting very much. I prefer going to school, particularly after I arrived at Brierley.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0033 }

“‘Respectfully yours, “‘Barbara Shaw.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0034 }

“Willie White’s started,
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0035 }

“‘Respected Miss,
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0036 }

“‘My desire is to inform you regarding my Very Brave Aunt. Ontario is where she resides, and on a particular day, she stepped outside to the barn, noticing a dog present in the yard. Because the dog ought not to have been there, she retrieved a stick, struck him forcefully, forced him inside the barn, and locked him in. Shortly afterward, an individual arrived searching for an inaginary lion’ (Query;—Was Willie referring to a menagerie lion?) ‘which had escaped from a circus. As it transpired, the dog was actually a lion, and my Very Brave Aunt had druv him inside the barn utilizing a stick. That she was not et up was a marvel, yet she possessed great bravery. Emerson Pettigrew claims that provided she believed it was a dog, her bravery was no greater than if it truly were a dog. Emerson, however, feels envy on account of not possessing a Brave Aunt of his own, having merely uncles.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0037 }

“‘The finest part has been saved by me for the end. You make fun of me because I believe Cedric to be a genius, yet I am confident his letter will persuade you that he is an exceptionally unusual child. Far down close to the beach, Cedric resides alongside his grandmother, and he lacks companions . . . no true companions. You recall that our professor of School Management informed us that we must refrain from having ‘favorites’ amongst our students, yet I am unable to prevent myself from loving Cedric Stanhope more than any of my others. However, I do not believe it causes any injury, since Cedric is loved by everyone, even Mrs. Sowerby, who claims she never would have thought she could become so attached to a Yankee. He is also liked by the other schoolboys. Nothing about him is weak or girlish, his dreams and fancies notwithstanding. He possesses great manliness and is capable of maintaining his position in every game. Not long ago, he engaged in a fight with St. Clair Trask on account of St. Clair asserting that the Union Jack was far superior to the Stars and Stripes as a flag. An undecided contest and a shared pact to honor one another’s patriotism from that point onward were the outcome. St. Clair remarks that the heaviest blows can be struck by him, but the most frequent ones can be landed by Cedric.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0038 }

“Cedric’s Letter.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0039 }

“‘My beloved educator,
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0040 }

“‘You informed us that we could send you letters regarding intriguing individuals in our acquaintance. In my opinion, the most fascinating individuals I am acquainted with are my rock people, and I intend to inform you regarding them. Other than grandma and father, I have not ever informed anyone else about them, but I desire to let you know about them since you comprehend things. A large number of people exist who fail to comprehend things, which makes it pointless to inform them.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0041 }

“‘By the water's edge reside my stone companions. Prior to winter's arrival, I was accustomed to visiting them nearly every nightfall. At present, I must wait until spring to go, yet they shall remain, because individuals of that nature do not ever alter . . . their unchanging nature is what makes them so wonderful. Nora was the earliest one among them I became friends with, which makes me feel I adore her most of all. Her home is in Pullen’ Cove, and black is the color of her hair and eyes, and she possesses complete knowledge regarding mermaids and water kelpies. She is capable of telling tales you really should listen to. Furthermore, the Twin Sailors exist as well. They lack a fixed residence because they are perpetually at sea, yet they frequently land to converse with me. They represent a couple of merry mariners who have witnessed all things within the world. . . and things beyond what exists in the world. Are you aware of what occurred to the younger Twin Sailor on one occasion? During a voyage, he navigated straight into a moonglade. Teacher, you are aware that a moonglade signifies the path a rising full moon casts across the ocean surface. Now then, the younger Twin Sailor traveled down this moonglade until he arrived directly at the moon itself, where he discovered a small door made of gold set into the moon, which he unlocked before sailing directly inside. Inside the moon he experienced remarkable exploits, but describing them here would render this letter excessively lengthy.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0042 }

“‘Furthermore, the cave holds the Golden Lady. A large cavern down by the beach caught my attention one day, so I entered it, discovering the Golden Lady after a bit. Falling all the way to her feet is her golden hair, and her gown shimmers and shines entirely like living gold. Playing all day on a golden harp, she produces music you can catch along the shore whenever you pay close attention, though the majority of folks would assume it was merely the wind passing through the rocks. Nora has never been told about the Golden Lady by me. Fear that it could cause her hurt feelings kept me silent. Talking too much with the Twin Sailors was enough to hurt her feelings.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0043 }

“‘My meetings with the Twin Sailors always occurred at the Striped Rocks. A very pleasant disposition belongs to the youngest Twin Sailor, whereas the oldest Twin Sailor is capable of looking terribly ferocious on occasion. Regarding that oldest Twin, I hold my doubts. Should he possess the courage, I think he would become a pirate. Something about him is truly quite enigmatic. Upon one occasion he used a curse word, so I informed him that a second offense would prevent him from coming onto the land to converse with me, since I had given grandmother my word that I would refrain from mingling with anyone who used bad language. You can take my word for it that he was quite frightened, and he stated that he would carry me to the sunset if I agreed to pardon him. Consequently, on the following evening as I sat upon the Striped Rocks, the oldest Twin came navigating across the ocean inside a magical vessel, and I stepped aboard. That vessel possessed a completely pearlescent and iridescent appearance, resembling the interior of mussel shells, while its sail looked like moonlight. Indeed, we navigated straight over to the sunset. Consider that, teacher, I have traveled inside the sunset. What might you imagine it to be? A land consisting entirely of blossoms makes up the sunset. We navigated inside a vast garden, where flowerbeds are formed by the clouds. We navigated inside a vast port, displaying the entire shade of gold, whereupon I walked directly off the vessel onto a large field completely carpeted with buttercups that were as large as roses. My stay there lasted for a very long period. Almost a year seemed to pass, though the Oldest Twin claims it was merely a matter of minutes. As you can tell, duration inside the sunset land lasts considerably longer than it does in this place.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0044 }

“‘Your affectionate student, “‘Cedric Stanhope.’
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0045 }

“‘P. S. teacher, naturally this letter is not actually accurate.
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0046 }

P.I.’”
{: #nw-v02-c11-p0047 }
